author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Evaluate a phone cooling accessory safely for PS2 emulation
summary: Compare passive baseline and accessory-assisted sustained routes at matched temperature, power, case, and fan settings, recording time-to-throttle and stability while avoiding condensation, blocked vents, and unsafe charging combinations.
heroAlt: Mobile phone beside a powered USB fan, illustrating safe accessory placement and cable checks

blocks.text: Measure time-to-throttle, not the coldest surface

A cooler is useful only if it extends stable gameplay without moisture, charging faults, blocked vents, uncomfortable handling, or excessive noise. Start with a passive baseline using a fixed ten-minute route. Repeat with one documented accessory level after returning the phone to the same starting condition. Record performance checkpoints and Android thermal status; do not treat a low external temperature as proof of safe internal operation.

Stop immediately on condensation, moisture, thermal warnings, unstable charging, swelling, painful surfaces, or unusual odor. Do not use freezer packs or operate below the accessory and phone manufacturers' safe conditions.

items: Phone and accessory instructions reviewed for placement and operating limits.
A dry room above dew-point risk with unobstructed device vents.
One fixed gameplay route long enough to reveal thermal decline.
Matched battery range, charging state, case use, brightness, and power mode.
A stable mount that does not press controls or strain the USB port.

blocks.text: Compare passive and assisted sustained curves

items: 1. Run the passive baseline from a documented cool idle state.
2. Record speed, frame time, thermal status, and surface observations at fixed intervals.
3. Stop, save the result, and allow the device to return naturally to baseline.
4. Mount the accessory as instructed and select one fixed cooling level.
5. Inspect for moisture before powering the phone or charger.
6. Repeat the identical route with no emulator or display changes.
7. Compare time-to-decline, low-percentile behavior, comfort, noise, and power stability.
8. Remove the accessory and inspect the phone and contact surface before normal use.

blocks.text: An accessory that delays the same late-session decline provides practical thermal headroom. A cooler opening minute without a sustained advantage is not enough. Recording noise, grip, port strain, and power behavior prevents a small timing gain from hiding poor everyday usability.
Accept the setup only when sustained behavior improves repeatably and every safety observation remains normal.

items: Both routes start from comparable thermal and battery states.
Accessory placement and level remain fixed.
No moisture, warning, charging fault, or unstable mount occurs.
Time-to-throttle or late-session frame time improves repeatably.
Normal controls, speakers, microphones, and vents remain unobstructed.
The assisted run also changes charging policy: split the variables.
Condensation appears: stop and dry the device according to manufacturer guidance.
A fan cable pulls on the phone port: redesign the mount before retesting.
Only a two-minute run is faster: repeat through thermal steady state.

blocks.text: Power down and remove the accessory, inspect and dry all contact surfaces, restore the normal case and charging arrangement, and let the device equalize before storage. Keep the conservative per-game profile even if the accessory provides optional headroom.
External cooling cannot override internal protections

Sensors, hotspots, battery temperature, and vendor control loops may react differently from the rear surface. Never bypass Android warnings or increase unsafe settings because a cooler is attached; use it only to improve margin within normal protections.
